craft_notes: Sthāyin: unborrowing opening. Sanskrit-first: svecchayā (BY-OWN-WILL — kept); anupādāna (NO-BORROWING — doubled no-hands/no-earth). Rows: 9 (no-borrowed-hands/no-borrowed-earth doubled), 7 (she — śakti blooms FEMININE, kept), 1 (‘opening’ closes — vikāsa last). Close: ‘in the opening’. Rupture: em-dash (will stated, then its unborrowing). Rejected: ‘opens’ for blooms — killed: blooms blooms (vikasana unfolds floral); ‘it’ for she — killed: feminine agent kept. Read aloud: BY-her-OWN-will SHE-blooms-it, ON-her-OWN-ground — NO-borr-owed-HANDS, NO-borr-owed-EARTH, IN the OPE-ning.

lines: By her own will she blooms it, on her own ground —
no borrowed hands, no borrowed earth, in the opening.

reads_against.argmap: How does free consciousness become the bound knower? → Cause stated, means refused, manifold explained, veil named: descent promised.
c1_essence: Free consciousness causes, unborrowing opens, divides by fitness, veils by tightening — descent promised.
